Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Money, work & business · Town, shops & places

merchant noun

also merchants, trader, dealer, wholesaler

classical

Cato Agr. praef. 3: mercātōrem autem strēnuum studiōsumque reī quaerendae exīstimō
Hor. C. 1.1.16

mercātor, mercātōris m.

noun, third declension

a merchant, a trader

Especially the wholesale trader who buys in bulk and ships goods, as against the retailer (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • negōtiātor, negōtiātōris m. — a businessman, a dealer

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Suet. Claud. 18.2: negōtiātōribus certa lucra prōposuit, he offered merchants a sure profit; Traupman 165: businessman

    A wholesale dealer or banker (Lewis & Short); see business.

Examples

  • luctantem Īcariīs flūctibus Āfricum mercātor metuēns ōtium et oppidī laudat rūra suī; mox reficit ratēs quassās, indocilis pauperiem patī.

    The merchant, afraid of the south-west wind wrestling with the Icarian waves, praises a quiet life and the fields of his home town; soon he is refitting his battered ships, unable to learn to put up with being poor.Hor. C. 1.1.15–18

  • Mercātōrem autem strēnuum studiōsumque reī quaerendae exīstimō, vērum, ut suprā dīxī, perīculōsum et calamitōsum.

    The merchant I consider energetic and keen to make money, but, as I said above, exposed to danger and disaster.Cato Agr. praef. 3

See also business, shopkeeper, seller, trade, market.

SourcesLewis & Short: mercator · Lewis & Short: negotiator
